extraction.text: The only difference between a triggered update and other update messages is the possible omission of routes that have not changed. The rest of the mechanisms about to be described must all apply to triggered updates.

answer_synthesis.description: Explain what this means in context.
answer_synthesis.explanation: Triggered updates are generated when there's a specific route change event (e.g., metric update, gateway change), and they include only routes that have actually changed. Normal updates are periodic broadcasts of all current routes regardless of changes.

answer_synthesis.technical_explanation: For triggered updates, routers mark route entries with a 'route change flag' when changes occur. When generating an update message, the router includes only those routes where the flag is set (i.e., routes that have changed). In contrast, normal updates (e.g., periodic broadcasts) include all routes in the routing table without filtering for changes.

The maximum datagram size of 512 bytes means triggered updates might split into multiple messages if many routes have changed, though this is not directly related to the key difference.

concise_summary: The key difference between triggered updates and other update messages in RIP is that triggered updates may omit routes that have not changed due to route change flags, while other updates always include all current routes.

Specifically, when a triggered update is generated, only routes with the route change flag set are included in the message. Normal update messages do not filter based on this flag and include all routes.
